Everything you need to ship from India to Suriname or import from Suriname to India: the trade agreement, routes and transit times, how your buyer imports, duties, regulators and documents.
India and Suriname at a glance
No trade agreement with India. CARICOM Common External Tariff applies.
India exports pharmaceuticals, rice and food products, vehicles, textiles and machinery. India buys timber and some gold. A large Indian-origin community drives demand for Indian goods.
Routes and transit times to Suriname
40–55 days via Caribbean or European transhipment (Kingston, Port of Spain, Rotterdam).
Transit times are indicative port-to-port from Nhava Sheva / Mundra (sea) and Delhi / Mumbai (air). Routing changes (for example Red Sea diversions) can add 10–14 days.
Importing into Suriname: what your buyer needs
Declarations are filed on ASYCUDA through a customs broker.
VAT (introduced in 2023) replaced the old sales tax.
CARICOM Common External Tariff, plus 10% VAT (some goods at other rates).

From Suriname to India, and tips from the field
File the Bill of Entry through a licensed customs broker in India (YAM holds licence R-7/92).
Check the HS code in the Indian tariff, the DGFT import policy (free, restricted or prohibited) and any BIS, FSSAI, plant quarantine or other permit before the goods ship.
If an agreement applies, get the correct certificate of origin from the exporter to claim the lower duty.
Amsterdam is a practical air hub: many Suriname flights connect through Schiphol.
